summary: Builds a row of single-character boxes for entering a one-time code, such as a verification code, with a blinking cursor in the active box and an optional dash separator.
purpose: Lets users type a short code one character per box.
why: Likely reason: one box per character is a common pattern for codes. The code does not state the exact reason.
how: It wraps the one-time-code input library in a styled container. It adds a group wrapper and a slot for each character. Each slot shows its character, highlights when it is active, and shows a blinking cursor when it is the current position. A separator shows a minus icon between groups. Everything is exported.
inputs: The code the user types, the slot index for each box, optional style overrides, and standard element settings.
outputs: A visible code entry row. The typed characters are passed to the screen through the library, which this file does not store.
risks: Each slot reads its state from the surrounding input component, so using a slot outside that component crashes it. A slot index that does not match the code length can break rendering.
debug: If slots show nothing, check that the slot indexes match the code length. If the cursor does not blink, check the animation style. If a crash mentions missing context, check that the slots sit inside the input component.
